conventions.absent_means: Value KOReader uses when the key is missing. isTrue/isFalse treat absent as false; nilOrTrue treats absent as TRUE (write false explicitly to turn off); readSetting(k, d) uses d.
conventions.effect: immediate = read at use time (e.g. checked_func, gesture handler); next_sleep = read in Screensaver:setup/show; next_book = read in a module/plugin init(), which runs when a ReaderUI (book) or the FileManager is (re)created; restart = read once at startup/module load. Note: G_reader_settings is held in memory and flushed on exit/suspend, so your plugin must write through the live G_reader_settings object and call G_reader_settings:flush(), never edit settings.reader.lua on disk while KOReader runs (it will be overwritten).
conventions.table_values: Entries marked type 'string' with a table default/notes 'Lua table' hold Lua tables; send them as JSON arrays/objects and convert. Dotted keys like footer.x / statistics.x / readtimer.x are fields inside ONE G_reader_settings key; merge, never replace blindly.
conventions.doc_defaults: copt_*/kopt_* are only defaults for books without their own saved values (sidecar overrides).

project_title.summary: Project: Title does NOT keep its settings in G_reader_settings. It stores them in its own SQLite database koreader/settings/PT_bookinfo_cache.sqlite3, table config(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT) (bookinfomanager.lua:74, 140). Writes go through BookInfoManager:saveSetting (bookinfomanager.lua:304): true is stored as 'Y', false as NULL (row with NULL value), numbers as text and parsed back with tonumber on load.
project_title.can_we_edit: Yes, but not via G_reader_settings:saveSetting. From inside KOReader (your plugin) the simplest safe route is to require Project: Title's BookInfoManager module and call BookInfoManager:saveSetting(key, value) — it keeps PT's in-memory cache in sync. Alternatively write the SQLite row directly (INSERT OR REPLACE INTO config(key,value)) while PT is not mid-query; PT only reloads settings on saveSetting/loadSettings, so a direct DB write takes effect after a KOReader restart.
